column1: # Golden vectors for the shared capture numbers and labels, read by both shells.
# (OpenCineAppKit); Kotlin keeps hand-written twins in `Android/media` and
# (Kotlin) assert every row, so a rounding or formatting rule that lands on one
# side only fails a test instead of reading differently per platform.
#   denom      degrees  fps          -> 1/N sent for a host-emulated angle (ties round up)
#   duration   num      den          -> MonitorCapturePresentation shutter label (C %g)
#   aperture   f-number              -> MonitorCapturePresentation iris label (one decimal, as every body)
#   ev         num      den          -> the one EV spelling (0.0, +0.3, U+2212 minus; C %.1f).
#                                       Rows with den 1000 are Nikon thousandths: the Swift Nikon
#                                       decoder must print them the same way.
#   rematch    degrees  angle  exposure  capture  prev  next  pending  available
#                                    -> 1/N a format change re-sends for a host-emulated angle,
#                                       `-` for no write: only manual video re-matches, never
